topic: Mixtures and Changes in Material Properties
key_concepts: A mixture is formed when two or more materials are combined without chemical reaction
No new material is formed in a mixture
Heterogeneous mixtures have materials that remain identifiable after mixing
Homogeneous mixtures have uniform appearance and materials can no longer be distinguished
Solid-solid mixtures can be heterogeneous or homogeneous depending on whether the material
Some solid materials dissolve in liquids while others sink or float
Soluble materials dissolve in water; insoluble materials do not
Hot water, stirring, and making materials smaller help solids dissolve faster
Some liquids mix completely with other liquids while others do not
Oil and water form a heterogeneous mixture because they do not mix
